query: FeCoNi is an fcc alloy with high saturation magnetization and a low coercive field. Earlier studies examined the high-entropy alloys FeCoNiPd and FeCoNiPt, but both exhibited soft ferromagnetism. A qualifying high-entropy alloy must have an almost equiatomic multicomponent composition and configurational entropy of at least 1.0R. Subject to these constraints, what single intervention could produce a FeCoNi-based high-entropy alloy with greater coercivity than the prior derivatives? Present one hypothesis that identifies the intervention, explains its mechanism, predicts the outcome relative to an appropriate FeCoNi-based baseline, defines the conditions over which it should apply, cites supporting observations from earlier work, and proposes a discriminating experiment with an explicit falsification criterion.

generation.hypothesis: Introducing near-equiatomic Al into FeCoNi (forming FeCoNiAl) will increase coercivity beyond that of previously studied FeCoNi-based alloys by promoting partial B2-type ordering and enhanced magnetocrystalline anisotropy, without compromising high configurational entropy (≥1.0R).
generation.material_initial_state: Baseline FeCoNi solid solution (fcc) with soft ferromagnetic behavior and low coercive field, restricted to equiatomic or near-equiatomic compositions.
generation.intervention: Substitute Al at ~25 at.% in an FeCoNi-based alloy, prepared by arc melting and homogenization, ensuring the total configurational entropy remains ≥1.0R.
generation.conditions: Near-equiatomic proportions for all principal elements (Fe, Co, Ni, and Al) and typical soft-magnetic processing temperatures below the disorder–order transition, to sustain the partially ordered B2 structure.
generation.structural_mediator: Partial B2 ordering and lattice distortion induced by Al, promoting grain/matrix interfaces that pin domain walls more effectively.
generation.mechanism: Local order enhances magnetocrystalline anisotropy and impedes domain wall motion by creating additional energy barriers, thereby raising coercivity relative to the baseline FeCoNi fcc alloy.
generation.predicted_outcome: A measurable increase (on the order of tens of percent or more) in coercive field relative to FeCoNiPd or FeCoNiPt, while maintaining a high-entropy single-phase or partially ordered structure and comparable saturation magnetization.
generation.baseline: Soft ferromagnetic FeCoNi-based alloys with low coercivity and high saturation magnetization, exemplified by FeCoNiPd and FeCoNiPt.
generation.boundary: The composition must remain near equiatomic to preserve high configurational entropy and single-phase (or partially ordered) stability; excessive non-equiatomic additions risk multiphase decomposition and loss of beneficial effects.
generation.uncertainty: The precise degree of B2 ordering and the magnitude of coercivity enhancement depend on thermomechanical treatments and quenching rates, which require further optimization.

falsification_experiment.design: Prepare a series of FeCoNiAl alloys by arc melting at near-equiatomic ratios, homogenize at ~1000–1100°C, then quench to retain partial B2 ordering. Compare with pure FeCoNi and FeCoNiPd/Pt references under identical processing.
measurements: X-ray diffraction or electron diffraction to confirm B2 superlattice reflections.
Magnetometry (hysteresis loops) to quantify any changes in coercive field and saturation magnetization.
Transmission electron microscopy to characterize lattice ordering and domain wall structures.
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the measured coercivity of FeCoNiAl does not exceed that of FeCoNiPd or FeCoNiPt under equivalent processing conditions, or if the alloy fails to remain near-equiatomic and single-phase (with a high-entropy configuration), then the hypothesis is falsified.

cited_evidence.text: While the AlCoFeNi high entropy alloy exhibits a single ordered B2 phase at high temperature, both the substitution of ferromagnetic Co with antiferromagnetic Cr, and lower annealing temperatures lead to a tendency for this system to decompose into a two-phase mixture of ordered B2 and disordered BCC solid solution. The length scale of this decomposition is determined by the combination of composition and annealing temperature, as demonstrated in this investigation by comparing and contrasting AlCoFeNi with the AlCo0.5Cr0.5FeNi alloy. The resulting phase stability has been rationalized based on solution thermodynamic predictions. Additionally, it is shown that replacement of Co by Cr in the AlCoFeNi alloy resulted in a substantial reduction in saturation magnetization and increase in coercivity. The microhardness is also strongly influenced by the composition and the length scale of B2 + BCC decomposition in these high entropy alloys.

AbstractStrong static magnetic field (SSMF) is a unique way to regulate the microstructure and improve the properties of materials. FeCoNi(AlSi)0.2 alloy is a novel class of soft magnetic materials (SMMs) designed based on high-entropy alloy (HEA) concepts. In this study, a strong static magnetic field is introduced to tune the microstructure, mechanical, electrical and magnetic properties of FeCoNi(AlSi)0.2 high-entropy alloy. Results indicate that, with the increasing magnetic field intensity, the Vickers hardness and the saturation magnetization (Ms) increase firstly, and then decrease and reach the maximum at 5T, while the yield strength, the residual magnetization (Mr) and the coercivity (Hc) take the opposite trend. The resistivity values (ρ) are found to be enhanced by the increasing magnetic field intensity. The main reasons for the magnetic field on the above effects are interpreted by microstructure evolution (phase species and volume fraction), atomic-level structure and defects (vacancy and dislocation density).Keywords: strong static magnetic field, high-entropy alloy, solidification, microstructure evolution, comprehensive properties

chosen.lever: introduce Al to generate local lattice distortions and partial B2 ordering
chosen.technique: arc melting and homogenization of FeCoNiAl in near-equiatomic proportions
chosen.conditions: maintain alloy’s high configurational entropy above 1.0R and measure coercive field under typical magnetic testing conditions
chosen.why: Adding Al at near-equiatomic proportions directly addresses the question of producing a higher-coercivity FeCoNi-based high-entropy alloy by breaking the full fcc symmetry found in FeCoNiPd or FeCoNiPt. Al promotes partial B2 ordering and local lattice distortions that can increase magnetocrystalline anisotropy and provide additional domain wall pinning, thereby enhancing coercivity while preserving the high-entropy alloy character. Arc melting plus homogenization is standard practice in the field, and measuring magnetic hysteresis under controlled thermal conditions can decisively test and potentially falsify this hypothesis.
